stem:
Kavya studies a branching-tree drawing in which each small branch looks like a smaller copy of the whole tree. She also looks at a plain oval with no smaller copies inside it.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: The plain oval is a fractal, because any closed curve counts as a fractal.
The branching tree is a fractal, because the same structure repeats at smaller scales.
The plain oval is not a fractal, because it has no self-similar smaller copies.
Only computer drawings can be fractals, so the branching tree is not one.

teacher.key_rationale: A fractal needs self-similar structure at smaller scales. The branching tree has it; the plain oval does not. Counting every closed curve omits that test. Restricting fractals to computer drawings over-narrows the idea.
